title: Unique Paths
oneLinerQuestion: Find the number of unique paths from top-left to bottom-right in an m x n grid.
explanation: Since movement is restricted to moving down or right, the number of paths to reach cell (i, j) is the sum of paths to (i-1, j) and (i, j-1). We solve this dynamically using a 1D DP array.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION uniquePaths(m, n):
    row = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(n, INITIAL_VALUE = 1)
    FOR i FROM 1 TO m - 1 DO:
        newRow = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(n, INITIAL_VALUE = 1)
        FOR j FROM 1 TO n - 1 DO:
            newRow[j] = newRow[j - 1] + row[j]
        END FOR
        row = newRow
    END FOR
    RETURN row[n - 1]
END FUNCTION

steps.narration: Line 2: Base case: top row cells can only be reached by moving right. row = [1, 1, 1].

Line 6: Cell [1][1] = left ([1][0]=1) + top ([0][1]=1) = 2 unique paths.
Line 6: Cell [1][2] = left ([1][1]=2) + top ([0][2]=1) = 3 unique paths. Row 1 complete.
Line 4: Row 2 start: cell [2][0] can only be reached from above. newRow[0] = 1.
Line 6: Cell [2][1] = left ([2][0]=1) + top ([1][1]=2) = 3 unique paths.
Line 6: Target cell [2][2] = left ([2][1]=3) + top ([1][2]=3) = 6 unique paths.
